name: linear-search
description: Same kind of linear problem, smaller (200 actions in R^10, 5 instances, 4 runs each). LinUCB and LinTS with theoretical values, then with the best alpha and lambda found on other seeds.

policies.label: LinUCB
notes: lambda_=0.1 (any lambda > 0 keeps the bound valid)
delta=0.01 (any delta in (0, 1): the bound holds with probability 1 - delta)

policies.label: LinTS
notes: delta=0.01 (any delta in (0, 1): the bound holds with probability 1 - delta)

policies.label: LinUCB searched
notes: lambda_=0.1 (any lambda > 0 keeps the bound valid)
delta=0.01 (any delta in (0, 1): the bound holds with probability 1 - delta)

policies.label: LinTS searched
notes: delta=0.01 (any delta in (0, 1): the bound holds with probability 1 - delta)

notices.title: Default hyperparameters
notices.text: Some policies used the **values from their papers**: alpha=1 for LinUCB; alpha=1, lambda_=1 for LinTS. The values of LinUCB searched and LinTS searched came from the grid search. LinUCB used the **OFUL radius** (Abbasi-Yadkori et al., 2011). These values are safe in theory. In practice, they often **explore too much**. The regret can then be higher than with tuned values.
notices.todo: Search the best values with param_grid=True. Or set them yourself, e.g. LinUCB(alpha=0.1).

notices.title: Grid search
notices.text: The hyperparameters of LinUCB searched and LinTS searched come from a grid search on this problem. The search tried 18 combinations, 2 runs each, on other seeds than the results. Each policy kept the combination with the best final regret. These values **fit this problem only**.
notices.default: No search: the values from the papers (param_grid=None).
notices.todo: Set your own grid, e.g. param_grid={"alpha": [0.1, 1]}. Set the runs per combination with search_runs (default 3).

notices.title: Values with no theoretical choice
notices.text: Some policies kept defaults with **no value from theory**: lambda_=0.1 (any lambda > 0 keeps the bound valid) for LinUCB; delta=0.01 (any delta in (0, 1): the bound holds with probability 1 - delta) for all policies. Other values can give a lower or a higher regret.
notices.default: These values (each policy's docstring explains them).
notices.todo: Search them with param_grid, e.g. param_grid={"lambda_": [...]}. Or set them, e.g. LinUCB(lambda_=1).

notices.title: Not stored
notices.text: This run **did not store** the pseudo-regret and the action of every step. The charts cannot show them.
notices.default: Regret, reward, CPU time and wall time only (track=(), measure_memory=False).

notices.title: Curves stored every 10 steps
notices.text: The curves kept one value every 10 steps. Between two kept steps, the line is **drawn, not measured**. You set log_interval=10.
notices.todo: Set log_interval=1 to keep every step. The files get larger.

notices.title: Slower timings
notices.text: Peak memory was measured (measure_memory=True). This made Python code about **5 times slower**. So the CPU times are higher than in a normal run.
